messages:
Samir K: Quick Q — for the private/edge deployments: are we still allowing aggregated telemetry out via the bastion to a customer S3 bucket? Concern is accidental PII/model traces escaping. Also how does our KMS envelope wrapping work for logs that flow through the bastion? If we need RBAC changes (sec-audit read), what's the minimal binding?
Lila Chen: Short answer: we push metrics to telemetry-sink inside the customer VPC by default. We try to scrub PII but model debug traces can slip through. For private installs we avoid sending raw request logs to public buckets. :no_entry_sign:
Marcus O: Which exact bucket/prefix are you worried about? if it's customer-owned S3 that's different than our central telemetry. For RBAC, prefer a service account with a scoped role + short-lived creds.
Samir K: bucket is customer-logs-123/prod-edge. Got a quick config snippet — is this the pattern we should restrict?
Samir K: ```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-except-telemetry
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: ["Egress"]
  egress:
    - to:
      - ipBlock:
          cidr: 10.0.0.0/16 # bastion/proxy
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 443
    - to: # allow kube-dns
      - namespaceSelector:
          matchLabels:
            k8s-app: kube-system
```
Priya R: That netpol looks fine as a baseline, but we need an explicit deny-all egress default rule in the tenant namespace. Also add egress to the local KMS endpoint only.
Marcus O: For KMS: use envelope encryption. Logs are encrypted with a per-tenant data key (DEK) and that DEK is wrapped by a CMK in the customer's KMS. Our service principal only gets kms:Decrypt for the wrapped DEK when the role is assumed. No persistent key material left on the node.
Samir K: Good — so RBAC change would be: create serviceaccount sec-audit-reader, bind to role audit-reader (list/get buckets, s3:GetObject for prefix), and grant STS assume-role to the short-lived creds flow?
Lila Chen: Yes. Minimal IAM policy example (customer-managed):
Lila Chen: ```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:GetObject"],"Resource":["arn:aws:s3:::customer-logs-123/prod-edge/*"]},
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["kms:Decrypt"],"Resource":["arn:aws:kms:region:acct:alias/tenant-cmk"]}
  ]
}
```
Marcus O: Also add CloudTrail + local audit agent shipping to the customer's SIEM (read-only), and lock retention to 90 days by default. If this is a vulnerability triage, we should open an incident ticket and flag as P1 if PII possibly leaked.
Samir K: Found a small leak pattern in logs where request metadata included user-id when debug=true. I've filed a vuln-triage issue: https://issues.internal/VT-442 — tagging @Priya R for remediation.
Priya R: On it. Immediate mitigation: patch logging to drop user-id, rotate DEKs for affected tenants, run a KMS rewrap for the impacted prefixes, and revoke the short-lived role tokens issued in the last 24h.
Samir K: deploy-bot FYI: can we schedule a canary rollout of the logging patch to one customer cluster first?
deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline queued — canary to edge-cluster-7 scheduled at 03:00 UTC. :white_check_mark:
Marcus O: Post-mortem checklist: 1) Confirm no external S3 access logs show unauthorized GETs. 2) Confirm DEK rewrap completed and CMK usage audited. 3) Update onboarding doc to ban raw request logs to external buckets.
Lila Chen: I'll add a short RBAC playbook for sec-audit-reader + netpol templates to the private-deploy runbook. Will also add KMS rewrap steps and an automated rotation script.
Samir K: Thanks all — appreciate fast replies. Keeping this thread for the remediation timeline updates.
